cards.note: Road 8B is a thin paved road (divided north of Chachapoyas) surrounded by distinct looking mountains. South towards the Cajamarca border the road runs along the edge of the mountain.
Mountains in this region are covered in green vegetation but have very visible rocky outcrops that give it a rugged appearance. These mountains are visible in most of the region.
Road 106 is a gen 4 dirt road in the Cordillera Blanca and is one of the most beautiful and easily recognizable roads in Peru.
Most of Peru’s snow-capped mountains are in the Cordillera Blanca mountain range in Ancash region, which also includes Peru’s highest peak, Nevado Huascarán.
Very foggy roads can be found in Ancash region, in the mountains west of Yungay.
Ancash region has hilly landscapes with lots of eucalyptus trees.
Landscapes with big, rugged mountain peaks (some covered by snow) can be found in the Cordillera Blanca mountain range in Ancash.
Road 30A cuts through a gorge. The entire road has overcast coverage, giving it a slightly dark appearance. The mountains are very recognizable.
Road 30B is a thin, paved road with distinct-looking pavement, having darker lines a bit like Texas pavement.
The town of Abancay is surrounded by tall, brown mountains with sparse vegetation, visible from most parts of the city.

The gen 3 coverage near Andahuaylas is tricky. The landscape looks lush, similar to Cajamarca. The combination of very overcast skies, black gen 3 car, and tall eucalyptus trees is a good clue for this area.
Road 3S in Apurimac, the main road between Ayacucho and Cusco, is a winding route along the edge of the mountains. Its elevated position overlooking a valley is a good indicator of Apurimac region.
Road 30A, between Nazca and Puquio, is a winding road passing through rugged, dry mountain ranges. Also these bollards are common along this road.
East of Puquio lies a vast, open plain of arid terrain. It is sparsely vegetated with low-lying brown and beige scrub. Much of the coverage is very overcast and appears a bit dark.
Road 30D through central Ayacucho is a thin, paved, high-elevation mountain road. The landscape is very barren, similar to roads in Huancavelica region.
Road 32 near Puquio is a thin mountain road. The northern section is a dirt road, while the southern section is paved. It has some bushes and shrubs, also rock walls are common along this road.

Cajamarca region has dense gen 3 dirt road coverage. Lush looking landscapes with lots of eucalyptus trees. Many houses have metal sheet roofs that reflect the sunlight. Often fields are fenced off by tree rows, similar to Ecuador and southern Colombia.
Cajamarca is hilly with lots of eucalyptus trees and more lush than regions in the south. Buildings often have overhanging roofs with wooden supports.
Cajamarca region at high elevation can have this unusual for the region looking grassland steppe with sparse vegetation.
Pine tree plantations are most common in Cajamarca region.
Cajamarca city can be identified by its abundance of northern-style roofs (overhanging with wooden supports) and white colonial-style architecture.
Recognizable mountain: Ausangate.
The town of Cusco has both red brick houses and white Spanish colonial-style buildings. It is surrounded by mountains. Buildings with orange or red tiled roofs are most common in Cusco region.
In southeastern Cusco, near the Puno border, there is a gradual transition between the rolling hills of the southern Altiplano and the slightly more forested landscapes of Cusco.
If you see steep, rugged brown mountains in a valley, you are probably in the Sacred Valley near Cusco, between Ollantaytambo and Pisac.

This gen 3 coverage, with a white (or almost blurred-out) Google car, very overcast skies, and a wintery feel (often with snow on the mountaintops), is found in southern Cusco region between Sicuani and the Arequipa region border.
The far southern part of Cusco region has gen 4 roads across landscapes similar to Puno’s Altiplano. Some of the roads are wide without road lines, others are unpaved.

Most of Huancavelica region has high-elevation roads with rugged, barren mountains. Many of the roads are thin, paved mountain roads with white outside lines and no middle line. Almost entirely gen 4 2025.
Eastern and northern Huancavelica region has a different landscape, with river valleys that are at a lower elevation and have a bit more vegetation, like bushes and shrubs.
Semi-urban landscapes with red soil dirt roads, some trees, prickly pear cacti, mud walls are common near the town of Huanta in northern Ayacucho region.
Huanuco region has gen 4 2024 rainy season coverage with lush hills and landscapes.
The city of Huanuco is surrounded by huge dark-green, barren mountains.
Unfinished roads (paved roads without road lines) are common in Huanuco region.
Huancayo can be recognized by the huge mountains surrounding the city, as well as its grid.
The valley between Huancayo and Jauja is a flat plain with trees, agricultural areas, and villages. It runs at a NNW angle and is surrounded by mountains.
Northern Junin, near Peru’s second-largest lake, has a more open landscape with rolling hills. This can look very similar to areas across the border in Pasco region.

Junin and Pasco regions are located on the central high-altitude plateau, featuring grassy hills with almost no vegetation and exposed rock. Puno region can look similar, but it has less exposed rock.
Gen 3 hilly landscapes with lots of eucalyptus trees. Often dirt roads. The landscape can look similar to Cajamarca but it’s a bit less lush. Black gen 3 car is most common.
Gen 3 mountain dirt roads with dry, yellowish-brown grass and small shrubs/bushes are most common in Lima region. The sky is also often hazy. Gen 3 black car is most common.
This unique concrete pavement exists only on Road 18 in Pasco and Lima regions.
Cerro de Pasco is a very high-elevation mining town. The buildings have metal sheet roofs, and the town is surrounded by rugged, barren mountains.
Lakes on a very open, high-elevation, hilly, and barren landscape can be found in western Pasco region.
Most of Pasco region lies on the central high-elevation plateau. The landscapes are similar to northern Junin: grassy plains with rolling hills and distant mountains.
Northern Pasco looks different from the rest of the region, featuring valleys through hills covered with eucalyptus trees.
Northern Pasco also has some higher-elevation gen 3 roads on hilly terrain with little to no vegetation.

Eastern Piura looks similar to Cajamarca region: hilly terrain, many eucalyptus trees, lush vegetation, and houses with northern-style roofs. Many roads in Piura are unpaved. Political logos can also help differentiate the two regions.
These bollards are unique to road 36A.
The southern part of Road 38 in Puno, which continues into Tacna region, is the only thin, paved gen 4 road in the region.
The only divided road in the region connects Puno and Juliaca.
Puno has many gen 3 roads across a flat, high-altitude grass plateau with small hills and few trees. Red brick houses and stone walls are also common.
Puno region is located on a high-elevation mountain plateau (altiplano) and can be recognized by vast grassy plains and rolling hills with sparse vegetation.
Juliaca is the largest town in the region and is flat, with a lot of red brick architecture. On gen 3 many of the roads inside the city are unpaved.
